bio: Senior Research Scientist Biostatistics, Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health Departments Department of Biostatistics I have worked as a Statistician on infectious disease clinical trials for over seventeen years; advancing statistical methodology, mentoring quantitative scientists and collaborating with numerous international investigators. My academic training and research experience have provided me with an excellent background in statistical theory, as well as study design, monitoring and analysis. As part of my master’s degree project, I conducted research using data from the UK HIV drug resistance database on the role of the HIV-1 subtype on response to antiretroviral therapy (ART). As a Statistician with the UK Medical Research Council (MRC) Clinical Trials Unit (CTU), my research focused on ART for HIV-infected children. Subsequently, I worked internationally in Chiang Mai, Thailand, and then came to Boston in the USA. I continually collaborated on infectious disease clinical trials. I was Senior Statistician for the iTAP clinical trial investigating tenofovir for the prevention of mother-to-child transmission of hepatitis B, and Senior Statistician for the antiretroviral strategies section of the NIAID-funded group for Advancing Clinical Therapeutics Globally for HIV/AIDS and Other Infections (ACTG).
